limitations: Static source evidence only; never a complete runtime import or call graph.
No target code, dependency installation, LLM, import hooks, or external API is executed.
Host Python grammar/stdlib and configured file, byte, entry and AST limits bound coverage.
Source-root candidates are conservative; runtime sys.path and packaging hooks are not evaluated.
Unknown external modules, dynamic imports/attributes, re-exports and wildcard symbols can remain unresolved.
Filename classifications are inferred; framework declarations do not prove runtime use or authentication coverage.
Literal defaults, annotation strings, route paths, arguments, assignment values and docstrings are omitted.
The caller must own a stable repository and prevent concurrent filesystem replacement.

guideline.title: FastAPI router boundaries
guideline.description: Use routers and dependencies when groups of endpoints need distinct organization or shared setup.
guideline.applicability: FastAPI imports are visible in the selected source evidence.
guideline.limitations: Small FastAPI applications may remain in one module. Routers alone do not establish authorization coverage.
benefits: Makes related routes and shared dependencies easier to review.
trade_offs: Additional modules can add wiring and navigation.

guideline.title: Keep architecture simple
guideline.description: Use the smallest design that addresses the demonstrated needs.
guideline.applicability: The selected graph is small or simplicity is an explicit requirement.
guideline.limitations: A bounded graph does not establish repository size. Separate boundaries can still be justified by ownership, risk, or deployment needs.
